subject: PO multi-SKU margin allocation and list-price clarify
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: PO multi-SKU private offer — margin allocation & list-price clarify

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the useful call earlier. Attached is a first-pass PO_Draft_APX.pdf with the three SKUs we discussed (metered inference, reserved throughput, and embeddings bundle). Before we lock numbers into the private offer, we have two operational questions where we need your input so we can align with CloudBridge and our finance team: 

1) List price vs private offer net: Does Apex require the Marketplace list price to match your internal sticker (public) price, or can we show a higher public list and deliver the negotiated net via the private offer? CFO flagged that public list price needs to reflect a stated per-unit for regulatory reporting, but procurement wants the net that appears on the invoice to match the committed spend in the PO.

2) Channel margin wiring: CloudBridge will be the reseller for part of the deal. Can you confirm whether Apex expects reseller commissions to be handled as a pass-through from Redwood (i.e., Redwood invoices at list, Redwood remits commission to CloudBridge) or whether you want commissions taken out of the private-offer net (effectively reducing Redwood's net revenue)? We want to avoid surprises on your side for revenue recognition and on ours for channel payouts.

Key asks / next steps: 
- Please confirm list-price requirement (matching public SKU or can differ).
- Confirm whether commissions should be structured as pass-through or netted from private-offer payout.
- If you have a target % for CloudBridge, share that so we can run the margin workback (I attached channel_margin_workback.xlsx).

I've looped in Lauren and Ben from our ops and partner teams to scope the mechanics once you confirm. If easier, we can jump on a quick 30-min call with CloudBridge tomorrow.

Thanks —

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0189

Attachments: PO_Draft_APX.pdf (3 pages), sku_list_and_rates.csv (CSV of candidate SKUs)

Subject: Re: PO multi-SKU private offer — margin allocation & list-price clarify

Sergio — thanks for sending. A few clarifications from our procurement / finance side: 

- Public list price: Our internal policy is that the public list price should be a reasonable published number for each SKU; it's okay if the private offer net differs as long as we can show the PO and the private-offer invoice for audit. In short: we prefer the list price to be present on the marketplace entry, but we do not require the invoice net to equal the public list.

- Channel commission handling: Preferably a pass-through model. We want CloudBridge to invoice/redline separately and get paid explicitly as a reseller commission so our audit trail is clear. CFO will push back if commissions are opaque in the net. If there are platform constraints that force commissions to be netted, please call that out now.

CloudBridge: we expect a 7% commission on consumption and a 4% commission on reserved capacity line items. Those are our starting points.

We can do a quick call tomorrow 10am PT if you need to walk through the draft.

—Maya
Director, Strategic Procurement | Apex Financials
Phone: (212) 555-6622

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding Apex's reply (below). Key points: Apex is OK with differing public list vs private net, but CFO prefers a clear pass-through for CloudBridge commissions. They suggested 7% consumption / 4% reserved.

Questions for ops/partners (Irene / Ben): 
- Can our AWS/GCP/Azure private-offer flow support an explicit pass-through commission line that CloudBridge invoices separately, while Redwood invoices Apex for the net? If not, what's the recommended implementation?
- If we must net, what's minimal concession we can offer while keeping deal economics intact? Show me a quick workback: list price anchoring -> private-offer discount -> reseller pass-through. I attached channel_margin_workback.xlsx for your inputs.

Also, legal asked whether DocuSign will need separate counterpart signatures for CloudBridge if they are a reseller on the PO. Leaning 'yes' but want to confirm.

Irene — can you weigh in on marketplace mechanics and whether any marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure) have a preference that would force us one way or the other?

Thanks,
Sergio

Subject: Re: Fwd: PO multi-SKU private offer — margin allocation & list-price clarify

Sergio / team — quick take from channel and finance side: 

1) Marketplace mechanics: AWS Private Offer and GCP Private Catalog both support offering a discounted private-offer price that differs from the public list price. Neither requires the public list to equal the private net. That covers the "list vs net" ask.

2) Commission handling: Both AWS and GCP tend to expect reseller commissions to be handled as a separate flow. In practice we do two patterns depending on partner capability: 
   - Pattern A (preferred): Redwood invoices Apex for the private-offer net. CloudBridge invoices Apex (or Redwood, per their contract) for the reseller commission. This is the cleanest for accounting and for Apex's CFO.
   - Pattern B (if partner can't invoice separately): Redwood invoices Apex at private-offer gross, then we calculate commission and remit to CloudBridge out of Redwood's payout. This requires Redwood to treat the commission as a contra-revenue / pass-through in our books.

Workback suggestion (attached): start with a public list that is ~10-12% above the negotiated private net so audits have a consistent sticker. If Apex is giving us a target net, we can reverse-engineer the public list for the SKU set. 

Numbers: using Apex's suggested 7% consumption / 4% reserved, the channel_margin_workback.xlsx shows Redwood net at ~89% of private gross on consumption lines and ~92% on reserved lines after commission if we do Pattern B. For Pattern A, Redwood reports full private gross and CloudBridge invoices/collects separately, so Redwood net equals private gross for recognition purposes.

3) DocuSign: CloudBridge will need to be expressly named on the PO if they are receiving commission from Apex; legal will want either a separate reseller addendum or a three-party acknowledgment. I'll coordinate with Legal.

Next steps: 
- I can finalize the workback (numbers) if someone from finance signs off.
- Sergio: confirm whether Apex prefers Pattern A (CloudBridge invoices Apex) — Maya's note leans that way. If Apex confirms, ops can proceed with private-offer setup with list-price anchor and a private net.

Ben
Channel Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: channel_margin_workback.xlsx (tabbed), sku_list_and_rates.csv
